replies.author: @TraceTheEarth
replies.text:
I lived in the Maldives for a while, and life there is indeed very different from the "paradise" imagery tourists usually see. While the blue seas and white sands are stunning, daily life is quite simple—and sometimes inconvenient—due to the islands being scattered far apart.

On inhabited islands, children attend school and residents shop at local stores; however, since many goods must be shipped from Malé or imported, prices are far from cheap. Basic healthcare is available, but serious medical issues often require travel to Malé for treatment.

Livelihoods primarily revolve around tourism, fishing, services, and local jobs. What stands out most in my memory is the much slower pace of life. Living in the middle of the Indian Ocean is beautiful, yet it reveals that the Maldives is not merely a giant resort; behind those picture-perfect beaches lies the ordinary life of small communities adapting daily to isolation, the weather, and the vast distances.

replies.author: @koo1150
replies.text:
As someone who actually lives in the Maldives, I can tell you it’s definitely not just beaches and coconut trees. We have pretty normal everyday life here too!
Almost every inhabited local island has its own school. Our literacy rate is around 98%. This rate is among the highest in the South Asia region. English is also widely spoken and understood. Especially among the younger generation.
We have boats that regularly transport food, groceries and other supplies between islands. Most islands have shops and basic services. Every local island has a health centre. There are also regional hospitals serving  different atolls. So you don’t necessarily have to come all the way to Male’ ( Capital) for everything.
Of course living on islands has its challenges. Especially transportation, bad weather and getting specialized medical care sometimes. But day-to-day life is quite normal. We work, go to school and colleges, grocery shops, eat out, use the internet, go to cafes. Basically everything people do anywhere else. 😊
